extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR tropical.lib (mathematicians / researchers / graduate students using SINGULAR for tropical geometry computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation and usage requirements for procedures in the SINGULAR library tropical.lib (procedures to compute tropical curves, Newton subdivisions, j-invariants, Weierstrass forms, t-initial forms/ideals, TeX output, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Input format for tropicalCurve
rubrics_metrics.description: tp is list of linear polynomials of the form ax+by+c with integers a, b and a rational number c representing a tropical Laurent polynomial; alternatively tp can be a polynomial in Q(t)[x,y] defining a tropical plane curve via the valuation map; the basering must have a global monomial ordering, two variables and up to one parameter!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure assumes the tropical polynomial is presented as the MINIMUM of the linear forms in tp unless the optional input #[1] is the string 'max'.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalCurve return structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list where each entry i=1,...,size(l)-1 corresponds to a vertex of the tropical plane curve and l[size(l)] contains Newton-subdivision data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed meaning: l[i][1]=x-coordinate, l[i][2]=y-coordinate; l[i][3]=intmat describing connections to other vertices and multiplicities; l[i][4]=list of primitive integer vectors + multiplicities for unbounded edges; l[i][5]=polynomial whose monomials mark the vertices in the Newton polygon corresponding to the entries in tp which take the common minimum at the ith vertex; l[size(l)][1]=boundary points of Newton subdivision; l[size(l)][2]=pairs defining interior edges of the Newton subdivision; l[size(l)][3]=intvec by which monomials in l[i][5] must be shifted if negative coefficients occurred in input.

rubrics_metrics.name: drawTropicalCurve input requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: f is list of linear polynomials of the form ax+by+c with integers a, b and a rational number c representing a tropical Laurent polynomial; alternatively f can be a polynomial in Q(t)[x,y] defining a tropical plane curve via the valuation map; the basering must have a global monomial ordering, two variables and up to one parameter!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same input format constraints as tropicalCurve.

rubrics_metrics.name: drawTropicalCurve behavior and options
rubrics_metrics.description: drawTropicalCurve(f[,#]) creates temporary TeX/PS files /tmp/tropicalcurveNUMBER.tex and /tmp/tropicalcurveNUMBER.ps and attempts to display the tropical curve via xdg-open; edges with multiplicity >1 carry that multiplicity; if # is empty curve computed w.r.t. minimum, if #[1] is 'max' computed w.r.t. maximum; if last optional argument is 'onlytexfile' then only the LaTeX file is produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to remove generated files call cleanTmp; lattice points black=marked, grey=not marked. The procedure requires a working LaTeX toolchain and texdraw.sty; errors like 'texdraw.sty not found' or missing xdg-open will prevent rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: drawNewtonSubdivision behavior and options
rubrics_metrics.description: drawNewtonSubdivision(f[,#]) creates /tmp/newtonsubdivisionNUMBER.tex and .ps files and attempts to display via xdg-open; if # empty, computes w.r.t. minimum; if #[1]=='max' computes w.r.t. maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lattice points in the Newton subdivision: black correspond to markings of the marked subdivision; grey are not marked. Requires LaTeX/texdraw and xdg-open to render; use cleanTmp to remove files.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalJInvariant input and basering requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: f is list of linear polynomials of the form ax+by+c with integers a, b and a rational number c representing a tropical Laurent polynomial; alternatively f can be a polynomial in Q(t)[x,y] defining a tropical plane curve via the valuation map; the basering must have a global monomial ordering, two variables and up to one parameter!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same input constraints as other tropical library procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalJInvariant return and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a number: if the graph underlying the tropical curve has precisely one loop then its weighted lattice length is returned, otherwise the result will be -1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the tropical curve is elliptic and its embedded graph has precisely one loop, the weighted lattice length is the tropical j-invariant; the procedure checks if the embedded graph has genus one but does NOT check if the loop can be resolved, so it may return a length even if the loop is resolvable; if the embedded graph has more than one loop the procedure may return -1 even if one loop remains after resolution. If # is empty compute w.r.t. minimum, if #[1]=='max' compute w.r.t. maximum. For plane tropical cubics the tropicalJInvariant equals the 'cycle length' defined in the cited paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: weierstrassForm input requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: wf is a polynomial whose Newton polygon has precisely one interior lattice point, so that it defines an elliptic curve on the toric surface corresponding to the Newton polygon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The characteristic of the base field should not be 2 or 3 (unless special cases); if an additional argument # is given a simplified Weierstrass form is computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: weierstrassForm return
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a polynomial: the Weierstrass normal form of the input polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm for the coefficients is due to Fernando Rodriguez Villegas (contact given). Examples show that weierstrassForm can remove cross terms depending on options.

rubrics_metrics.name: jInvariant input and optional argument semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Input f is a polynomial whose Newton polygon has precisely one interior lattice point so it defines an elliptic curve; optional argument # (when base field is Q(t)) may be 'ord' or 'split'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'ord' returns an integer (the order of the j-invariant). 'split' returns a list of two polynomials whose quotient is the j-invariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: jInvariant return and field-characteristic caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a polynomial: the j-invariant of the elliptic curve defined by the polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic of base field should not be 2 or 3, unless the input is a plane cubic. If base field has parameter t, jInvariant(...,'ord') computes the order which may be compared with tropicalJInvariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: conicWithTangents input requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: points is a list of five points in the plane over K(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The points must be generic, i.e. no three on a line.

rubrics_metrics.name: conicWithTangents return structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list l with: l[1]=the list points of the five given points; l[2]=the conic f passing through the five points; l[3]=list of equations of tangents to f in the given points; l[4]=ideal, tropicalisation of f; l[5]=list of the tropicalisation of the tangents; l[6]=list containing vertices of the tropical conic f; l[7]=list containing lists with vertices of the tangents; l[8]=string with LaTeX code to draw the tropical conic and its tropicalised tangents; l[9]=if # non-empty, same data for the dual conic and dual points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shows indexing and content of each entry; write out conic[8] to a file and process with latex/dvips/xdg-open to visualise (requires TeX toolchain and xdg-open).

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalise input and valuation option
rubrics_metrics.description: f is a polynomial in Q(t)[x1,...,xn].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tropicalise(f[,#]) returns the linear forms of the tropicalisation of f. If # is empty, valuation of t is 1; if # is the string 'max' it will be -1 (meaning consider maximum of linear forms instead of minimum).

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicaliseSet input and return
rubrics_metrics.description: tropicaliseSet(i) takes i an ideal in Q(t)[x1,...,xn] and returns a list where the jth entry is the tropicalisation of the jth generator of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to tropicalise all generators of an ideal; examples illustrate returned linear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: tInitialForm definition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: tInitialForm(f,w) for f in Q[t,x1,...,xn] and integer vector w=(w0,w1,...,wn) returns the t-initialform of f(t,x) w.r.t. w evaluated at t=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The t-initialform is the sum of the terms with MAXIMAL weighted order with respect to w.

rubrics_metrics.name: tInitialIdeal usage
rubrics_metrics.description: tInitialIdeal(i,w) for ideal i in Q[t,x1,...,xn] and intvec w returns the t-initial ideal of i with respect to w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows that the t-initial forms of generators need not generate the t-initial ideal; the procedure computes the full t-initial ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: initialForm definition
rubrics_metrics.description: initialForm(f,w) for f in Q[x1,...,xn] and w=(w1,...,wn) returns the initial form of f(x) w.r.t. w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initialForm consists of terms with MAXIMAL weighted order with respect to w.

rubrics_metrics.name: initialIdeal definition
rubrics_metrics.description: initialIdeal(i,w) for ideal i in Q[x1,...,xn] and intvec w returns the initial ideal of i with respect to w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initialIdeal consists of terms with MAXIMAL weighted order w.r.t. w; examples illustrate output.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX output: texNumber
rubrics_metrics.description: texNumber(f) returns a string: TeX command representing leading coefficient of f using \frac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: texNumber((3t2-1)/t3) -> '\tfrac{-1+3\cdot t^{2}}{t^{3}}'. Useful to generate LaTeX representation of coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX output: texPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: texPolynomial(f) returns a string: the TeX command representing polynomial f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example output uses \tfrac and \cdot with superscripts; used to embed polynomial in LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX output: texMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: texMatrix(M) returns a string: the TeX command representing matrix M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces a LaTeX array environment representing entries; example shows formatting of mixed numeric and polynomial entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: texDrawBasic input and return
rubrics_metrics.description: texDrawBasic(texdraw) takes texdraw a list of strings representing texdraw commands (as produced by texDrawTropical) and returns a string: a texdraw environment enclosing the input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: texDrawBasic is called from conicWithTangents; produced environment must be processed by LaTeX to generate graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: System dependencies for LaTeX rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures that produce LaTeX/PS (drawTropicalCurve, drawNewtonSubdivision, conicWithTangents, tex outputs) assume a working LaTeX toolchain (latex, dvips), texdraw.sty present, and an opener (xdg-open) to display output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If texdraw.sty is missing LaTeX will error ('texdraw.sty not found'); if xdg-open is absent the produced PS/PDF will not be automatically displayed. Use 'onlytexfile' option when xdg-utils not installed, and cleanTmp to remove /tmp files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global cross-cutting option: min versus max
rubrics_metrics.description: Across many procedures (tropicalCurve, drawTropicalCurve, drawNewtonSubdivision, tropicalJInvariant, etc.) the default is to compute with respect to the MINIMUM of computed linear forms; if the optional argument #[1] is the string 'max' then computations use the MAXIMUM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the desired convention (min vs max) via the optional argument to ensure consistent tropicalisation and graph computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genericity requirement for geometric constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Points input to geometric routines (e.g., conicWithTangents) must be generic: e.g., no three of the five points should lie on a line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-generic input may cause incorrect or degenerate outputs; examples and notes stress this constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field characteristic caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: For weierstrassForm and jInvariant the characteristic of the base field should not be 2 or 3 (unless the input is a plane cubic in some cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These algorithms assume characteristic ≠ 2,3 for correct coefficient computations; take care when working over small-characteristic fields.
